newsitem.title: USA: USDA lists U.S. farm export subsidies since July 1.
newsitem.headline: USDA lists U.S. farm export subsidies since July 1.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department said Friday the United States subsidized export sales of 420 tonnes of nonfat dry milk since July 1, with a total subsidy of $383,000.
July 1 was the date that subsidy quantity limitations began under the World Trade Organization.
Some 44 tonnes of whole milk powder was exported under subsidies worth $44,000 in the same time period. Subsidized cheese sales were 88 tonnes, with a subsidy value of $85,000.
No subsidies were made on feed grains, wheat, frozen poultry, rice, vegetable oil, eggs or butterfat since July 1, USDA said.

Since October 1, 1995, the date monetary support restrictions began, the values of U.S. subsidies were as follows: frozen poultry $5.153 million; nonfat dry milk $16.818 million; whole milk powder $1.551 million; cheese $2.056 million. Subsidies on other agricultural categories were zero.
